problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨6{x}^{2}+2y,\,-10y-\operatorname{arctan}⁡x⟩
$$

through the boundary of the triangle with vertices $(0,0),(2,1),$ and $(-2,1).$

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating Flux Across Other Type I and Type II Regions
examples.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
\mathbf{F}(x,y) = \left\langle -3xy^2 , \: y+\cos x \right\rangle
$$

through the boundary of the triangle with vertices $(0,0), (2,2),$ and $(-2,2).$
examples.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $\mathbf F = P\,\mathbf i + Q\,\mathbf j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
\oint\limits_C \mathbf F\cdot\mathbf n\,\textrm d s = \iint\limits_D \textrm{div}\,\mathbf F\,\textrm{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
\oint\limits_C P \,\mathrm{d}y - Q \, \mathrm{d}x = \iint\limits_D \left( \dfrac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \dfrac{\partial Q}{\partial y} \right) \,\textrm{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062447/assets/aa822f0b9259d6d9eb5c6f439588e70d4b9bee16b2b868fae36c7cbac72d3c3f.png)

We have that $P(x,y) = -3xy^2$ and $Q(x,y) = y+\cos x .$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=-3{y}^{2},\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type II region as follows:

$$
D = \left\{(x,y) :  -y \leq x \leq y, \, 0 \leq y \leq 2 \right\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-3{y}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{-y}^{y}(-3{y}^{2}+1)\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(-3{y}^{2}+1)[x]_{-y}^{y}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(-3{y}^{2}+1)(y-(-y))\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(-3{y}^{2}+1)\cdot 2y\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{2}(-6{y}^{3}+2y)\,dy \\  & =[-6\cdot \frac{{y}^{4}}{4}+2\cdot \frac{{y}^{2}}{2}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =[-\frac{3{y}^{4}}{2}+{y}^{2}]_{0}^{2} \\  & =(-24+4)-0 \\  & =-20.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Use the flux form of Green's theorem to calculate the flux of the vector field

$$
F(x,y)=⟨{e}^{y}+2{x}^{2}y,\,{e}^{x}+2x{y}^{2}⟩
$$

through the boundary of the rectangle with vertices $(-1,0),(2,0),(2,1),$ and $(-1,1).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $F=P\,i+Q\,j,$ and $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first derivatives on an open region containing $D,$ then the flux form of Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s={∬}_{D}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}A,
$$

which is equivalent to

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\,\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14062447/assets/f6437eddec7d44a10c7fb2b3461a09844ca06e5131b69503f51432eb87fedd31.png)

We have that $P(x,y)={e}^{y}+2{x}^{2}y$ and $Q(x,y)={e}^{x}+2x{y}^{2}.$ So,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂x}=4xy,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂y} & =4xy.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the rectangular region $D$ as follows:

$$
D={(x,y):-1\le x\le 2,\,0\le y\le 1}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's theorem in flux form, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}F\cdot n\,\text{d}s & ={∮}_{C}P\,dy-Q\,dx \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂P}{∂x}+\frac{∂Q}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(4xy+4xy)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{-1}^{2}8xy\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}4{x}^{2}y\,{|}_{-1}^{2}\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(4(2)^{2}y-4(-1)^{2}y)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}(16y-4y)\,dy \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}12y\,dy \\  & =6{y}^{2}\,{|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$
